items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name — she volunteered 'my name is Priya' and he never acknowledged or used it once the entire call
No 'How are you today?' and no agenda statement or 'sound good?' confirmation
Opened the discount question with a flat 'No, we don't have any additional discounts' before any value reframe
No No Worries Damage Coverage mention ($2,000 accidental damage) — insurance never came up at all
No Meet Your Mover email description
No On-Time Guarantee — gave an 8:30-9:00 arrival window but never said Einstein discounts if it misses the window
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Clock mechanics incomplete — explained 15-minute increments but never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never mentioned the 2.5-hour minimum
Never stated number of movers or trucks on the 6-hour estimate
Gave a flat '6 hours' with no typical time range for a 2BR apartment, even after the customer said another rep told her 4.5-5 hours
No 'does that make sense?' close after the Save Your Ass speech — and the customer had already said 'the increment kind of, I don't understand'
No 'reply with any corrections' / BOLDED email detail list explained
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave hours or how to reach us

Zero probing beyond what was already on the profile — no packing, boxes, storage, additional stops, additional rooms, access/parking, or moving stressors; the customer had to volunteer the second-floor lift herself
top_strength: The Save Your Ass speech was genuinely strong and unprompted — he tied prep directly to money ('the more time we can save you'), gave real consolidation examples (lamps, hanging clothes, photos), and offered the take-a-carload tip. He also handled the 'what if we finish sooner' question cleanly with a concrete example (5 hrs 15 min = pay 5 hrs 15 min).
coaching_note: Rance is treating the confirmation call as pure order-taking — he read the profile back and closed, but skipped every differentiator. Add No Worries, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee to booking calls; on this one he already had the customer sold, so those 60 seconds cost nothing and would have justified the price she was trying to negotiate down.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and competent but transactional — never used her name, answered the discount and time-change asks bluntly ('No, I mean...'), and offered no affirmations or empathy, though the customer stayed positive and booked.
